prompt: Same graph: $g$ is the line $y = 2x + 1$, except that at $x = 2$ there is an open circle on the line and a solid dot at $(2, 7)$. What is $g(2)$?
hint: $g(2)$ asks for the actual output at $x = 2$ — look for the SOLID dot, not the open circle.

hints.text: $g(2)$ asks for the actual output at $x = 2$ — look for the SOLID dot, not the open circle.
An open circle means "the graph is not here." A solid dot means "the graph IS here."
The solid dot sits at $(2, 7)$, so $g(2) = 7$.

explanation: The value of a function at a point is read off the solid dot.
At $x = 2$ the solid dot is at height $7$, so $g(2) = 7$.
Compare: the limit there is $5$. Limit and value can disagree — that is exactly what a hole with a dot looks like.

alternativeExplanations.title: Two different questions
steps: "What is $g(2)$?" means: stand exactly at $x = 2$ and look up. You see the dot at $7$.
"What is the limit?" means: walk toward $x = 2$ and watch the height. You see the line heading to $5$.
A function is only continuous when both answers match. Here they do not.
